utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you asked for a couple of minutes yesterday, and could it be done in open session? We have -- we -- yesterday, we finished in closed session. I think at this moment we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think it would be better if we did it in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session. Just for the sake of the transcript, I think it is good to have in the transcript at this moment an observation by myself which is that during the closed session, we dealt with issues that should be dealt with in closed session, but we also dealt with objections made by the Defence regarding the way of objections made by the Prosecution during the examination-in-chief of witnesses. And the Prosecution has responded that. It should have been done in open session. I think that there is no need to repeat it, but for the transcript, I think it is good to establish that this has been a discussion. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, only a matter of the form. I am not talking formally about the objections of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objections coming late and not objection against --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...the answers where the Prosecution indicated that it was not always possible to object against the questions because only from the answers it became clear that there was lack of relevance, according to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Ms. Pilipovic, you could now call the witness DP6 again. Should we have to start in closed session or do you think that we can start now in open session? The protective measures, of course, being effective.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Thank you, Your Honour. We can begin in open session and when necessary, I will ask that we go into a private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So then I see the usher left the courtroom already in order to escort the witness in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning. Please be seated, Mr. DP6.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave yesterday. Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Pilipovic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, you told us yesterday where you were born and where you lived. The time of interest to the Defence is 1992, 1994, specifically, I am asking you about September of 1992. Where were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: September 1992 I was in Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us when you say that you were, where exactly were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Lukavicka Cesta, Lukavicka Road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in what capacity were you there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a company commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us as a company commander at Lukavicka Cesta, this company was about what formation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Infantry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What larger unit did you belong to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Infantry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How strong was the company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the beginning we were over 100, but then the numbers steadily decreased.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your company was part of which brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Ilidza Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where was the command post of your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Lukavicka Cesta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us when was your company put together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It came into being after the withdrawal of the former Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us when was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure of the exact date, but I know it was sometime in May, late May, June, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that it was formed in late May or June, can you briefly tell us how and why was your unit formed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our unit was formed -- at first we were something like Territorial Defence and we were defending our homes. And we practically organised ourselves. But when the Yugoslav People's Army withdrew, it was then that within the battalion the company was formed too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, if I understand your answer, before the pullout of the Yugoslav People's Army you were organised in the Territorial Defence. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us when was that when were you organised in the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was following the 4th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you organised the Territorial Defence following the 4th of April, 1992, can you tell us whether you were armed as the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the Territorial Defence in the beginning, we had the hunting weapons and pistols of sorts. And later on after the barricade, the first weapons we had were the weapons when the police came, and we disarmed those police. And after the barricades, the police split up too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP, when you talk about the organisation of the Territorial Defence, you are talking about the organisation within the locality that you lived in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us at that locality how many inhabitants did it have that 1992, in April, May, 1992, therefore?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well I am not quite sure, but I say 1.000, perhaps 1.200.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you have any direct knowledge, can you tell us something about the ethnic structure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Nedzarici, 95 per cent of its inhabitants were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You keep telling us that you organised first the Territorial Defence and then that you acted within a company that is a battalion in that part of your neighbourhood. Can you tell us why did you organise yourselves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We organised ourselves because the police was split up at the time, and as one walked around the city before the barricades, there were some Green Berets. And we had to organise ourselves in the Territorial Defence for our safety sake, that is, for our safety, our children's safety, and our home's safety.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if there were ever any incidents specifically since you are talking to us about organisation in April, May, June 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was shooting, shooting started across the positions, at the positions where we were when we organised ourselves as the Territorial Defence. At first, shooting started. As days went on, there was more and more shooting. Muslims started provoking from the other side, started shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP, later on at closed session, I will ask you to point exactly where you were. But now, could you tell us about your company that you were the commander of. How many platoons did it have, or rather did it have any smaller units within its structure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were these units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were platoons and then they were divided into sections.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just told us now that the sections were divided into trenches. Are you telling us that on the position where your company was there were trenches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the moment when we organised, of course we had to make some shelters because of the shooting from the other side. And these were trenches and these trenches were in houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I have to intervene because there is a part of the French transcript which is not interpreted. I apologise, but "they were divided into sections." And this part was not in the French interpretation, and then after sections, we are talking about trenches, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, I would just like to ask you to look at the screen in front of you. And as soon as the cursor starts, could you then start talking, because we are speaking the same language, so it could create a problem with the interpreters. Mr. DP6, could you tell us when were these trenches dug in the area of your company, so to speak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The digging of the trenches happened -- I don't know exactly what the date was, but it was in May after the JNA withdrew. And the reason why it happened, it is because there were already people who were injured and people who were killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "there were already people who were injured and people who were killed," could you tell us where were people killed and injured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the Lukavicka Cesta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, could you tell us, what was the width or what was the length rather of the front line of your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The length of our front line or the width of our front line in certain places, only a street divided us. And in some other places, there was perhaps 20 or 30 metres. These were very close lines. Sometimes just a street, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP, perhaps there was a misunderstanding. I asked you about the length of the front line of your own company.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The length of the front line of my company was approximately 500, 600 metres [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the depth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The depth of the front line was 3, 4, 500 metres [as interpreted]. I can't tell you exactly. It depended on the place. Because Nedzarici was completely surrounded, so it really depended on the place, depending on which specific spot on the line we were looking at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us when we are talking about the period when you organised yourself as a TO and later on as a company, how were you armed and how were you dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To start with, we were dressed in uniforms of the JNA, not all of us. There were some of us who were in ordinary clothes. Later on, later on we received some camouflage uniforms, but that was already summer by then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you had different weapons and some of them in uniforms of the JNA and some of them, as I understood it, in civilian clothes, could you tell us the uniforms of the JNA, how did you have them? How did you come by them? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the JNA withdrew, we entered the barracks, took the uniforms, and put them on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, these barracks, where was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was located next to the Aleja Branka Bujica Street. It is in the direction of Stupska Brdo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling us that this was in your locality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, as a company commander, what weapons did you have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had infantry weapons. We had M-48 rifles, semi-automatic rifles, automatic rifles, and that was it. And we had M-53 semi-automatic machine-guns, old ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now that you have told us all this, could you tell us, how did you come by these weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We got the weapons from the barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain to us how come that you had these weapons from the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened when the JNA withdrew. We entered the barracks, we took the weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say, "we entered," could you tell us who and how many of you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we entered practically we went into groups. And -- in groups, and we were just taking these weapons. I can't tell you exactly how many there were of us, whether we were in groups of 10 or 15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anyone in the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, in the barracks probably there was someone, but I don't know who it was. There was someone, but when the JNA withdrew, the barracks were practically empty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within your company or, if you know, within the battalion, were there professional military personnel from the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if you have served in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what is your military specialty.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am anti-aircraft, light anti-aircraft, artillery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, you told us about the positions of your company, how many people were there, how you were dressed, and that you were in trenches. Could you tell us something else. You told us that the second line, the opposite line that was opposed to you, was about 4, 5 metres away from you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 4 or 5 metres, yes, because they were in a residential buildings. And on the other side we were in the -- in our own houses where they were not large residential buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say they were in residential buildings, could you describe for us in relation to your street, in comparison to your line, to your front line, what were these buildings like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were several multi-storey buildings, six, seven six to ten storeys, it depended which building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that they were in buildings, could you tell us who was in the building? Did you see them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslim soldiers were in buildings. And occasionally we saw them, but we couldn't see them very often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us from the other side, were there trenches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, there were. Their trenches were in buildings, just like our trenches were in our houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I would be grateful if my learned colleague could take me to the reference where the witness said that the line that was opposed to him was 4 or 5 metres away. I simply don't recall it; I can't find it. And I apologise if it is there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my colleague is usually reacting after the answer. My question was about the width of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. front line. I can't come back to that now, I can't find it in the transcript, but the witness was explaining about the width of the front line. And I told him that it was a misunderstanding. I was asking about the front line, the length of the front line of your company. And this is then that Mr. DP6 spoke about the distance of 2 or 3 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have the --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If this is a problem, Your Honour, perhaps you could ask the witness if that is what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, in my transcript, I think there was a different -- different testimony. I had, as a matter of fact, in my recollection on page 13, line 16, the answer was "the depth of the front line was 3, 4, 500 metres." That is what the transcript says. So I was a bit surprised as well. And if you say that the objection came late, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And before that, he said that it wasn't that spot. It is before "3, 400 metres." That was precisely my question. It was before the witness spoke --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was 20 to 30 metres is what he said, according to the English transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I know for sure that the witness said that the front line where it was divided was just a street but we can ask the witness in order not to waste time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He said a street, that's correct, one street, but in the transcript, at least, I cannot read 2 to 3 metres. Perhaps you clarify this. I think, as a matter of fact, that it is -- if the objection came late, that it is always good, first, to check carefully what you read in the transcript. So, therefore, since this was a bit confusing, I noticed it myself as well, that we should not blame the other party for first checking the transcript before pointing at a confusing issue. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, can you tell us how far was the front line of the other side from you and according to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were just a street away from each other. The width of that street was 3, 4 metres, depending, of course. It wasn't more than 3 or 4 metres between the buildings and where we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, can you tell us, bearing in mind the width of your front line, in relation to the depth of the -- the width of your front line and the other front lines, was the difference always so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I explained, in some places it was 3 or 4 metres, and there was -- there could also be a distance sometimes 20, 30, 40 metres. I can't tell you exactly what it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you throughout - all along your line, did you have trenches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout the line at certain distances we had trenches, and these trenches were located in our houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP, if the Defence showed you the map of the city of Sarajevo, the plan of the city of Sarajevo, would you then be able to indicate and mark on this map the lines of both sides, and then show to us in which part of the Lukavicka Cesta was your front line located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before I show you this map, could you tell us the other side that you say were in buildings. On the other side of the front line, were there all buildings, and if there were, what was their height?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all buildings, and these buildings were 6, 10, 12 storeys. I didn't count the storeys. But they held on to their positions in these buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that "they held on to their positions in these buildings," could you tell us in the period 1992 September to August 1994, from your positions was there firing and from which weapons, and also was there firing from the other side? Could you describe to us the situation on the line where you were a company commander.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On a daily basis on these lines, there was firing. As for the weapons, we had, as I explained earlier, M-48 semi-automatic rifles, automatic rifles, and we had the M-53 semi-automatic machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that there was shooting on a daily basis --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- can you describe for us one event, one incident, during the day. Could you describe how it happened.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This happened in the following way: Muslim soldiers would start shooting, would start provoking, and we just responded. We were just returning fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to see from which positions the soldiers from the other side were firing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From which positions were they firing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were firing from the buildings as I have described. They were firing -- they were firing from weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to see the weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I was not able to see the weapons. But it was weapons -- were weapons. And I could see where the fire was coming from, from which buildings the fire was coming from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us was there a specific location where there was constant firing or did these locations change?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were locations, and they did change because they had buildings because they were multi-storey buildings. And then were able to change their firing positions. And they knew -- we knew sometimes which buildings they were firing from. It was possible to see -- it was possible to hear where the firing was coming from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, I am going to show you a city map, plan of the city. Later on, I will show you some other maps, but perhaps you can explain to us what were these buildings in question and what the line was and which street this was on.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I marked the map of the city D1760. Your Honour, bearing in mind that Mr. DP6 will be putting in positions, perhaps it would be a good idea to go in closed session, because in these questions, I would like to ask some other more specific questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session. And just for the sake of the transcript, and looking at the map that is on the ELMO, I indicate that the witness DP6 has just marked on a map in the area of Nedzarici where his front line was, which is a continuing black line, and where the front line of the opposite party was, that is a dotted line quite close to it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, you were about to explain to us the structure of buildings on the side of -- manned by -- held by the BH army, and you started telling us about the shopping centre.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the shopping centre right here. These are tall buildings here, six-storey buildings. And to about this place, and the buildings which are in this part here are not less than ten storeys high. Between them, there is a clearing; there was nobody there because it was open. And then there is the health centre, the Arandjelovac building as they called it. The soldiers were in it to. They slept there, spent time there, and also fired from it. Then at the foothills of Mojmilo, there were also other buildings. These are these houses and that is where they also where and fired from.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for the transcript, the Defence would like to say that the witness explained that the dotted line are buildings, more than six storeys high, that is ten-storey building. Then marked with the red crosses, that is where the buildings are, the health centre, and that is where the troops of the BH army also were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, you tell us -- how tall were the buildings at the front line? The tallest building, how tall was the tallest building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were in small family houses, so you would have a ground floor and the first floor. So our buildings were perhaps 5, 6 meters tall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us at what time did you hold these positions? We said -- we talked about April, May 1992. You said September 1992. Until when were you there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the 20th of February, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say, "20th of February, 1993," when you were wounded; is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you return to that place again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1993, I returned from the hospital, or rather, I first went to the Arandelovac spa. And then after Arandelovac sometime in October, I joined by battalion again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you continue to command the company after October 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, we shall now talk about the time before February 1993 when you were wounded. Did you have any knowledge --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I may have a problem with the English transcript. As I understand the evidence, the witness was in that position until the 20th of February, was then wounded. Question: "Did you return to that place again?" "In 1993 I returned to the hospital and so on." Next question: "And did you continue to command the company after October 1993?" There is no reference to October in the English transcript, so I would be grateful if we would have the translation of what the witness said about October of 1993. I am unclear as to what happened. Alternative, perhaps my friend could lead it from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will ask the witness --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, when did you return? You told us that you were wounded in February 1993? When did you go back to that place, that is, the positions where your home was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I was wounded you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the wounding, I returned to the battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I returned in October. In September, I left the spa. I didn't join by battalion straight away because I was still not quite well. And I came to my battalion in October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as of October 1993, you were again at that location and until when were you there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From October 1993, and how long did you stay on that line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- after October, I was not at Lukavicka Cesta front line. I was in the rear -- in my brigade's rear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. DP6. Mr. DP6, let us talk now about the time when you were not wounded. Can you tell us if you had information, did you have any direct knowledge of how many soldiers were on the side of the BH army in relation to the front line of your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, I do not know how many of them there were. But I know that there were -- that I -- outnumbered us by far. One could see it from -- one could deduce it from their attacks, from the number of their attacks they carried against Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say one could deduce from their attacks. Can you tell us how frequent were these attacks? When I say "how frequent," I mean by per day, per week, per month. Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those attacks were a daily occurrence. Nedzarici was attacked every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, did you, from your positions which you held, see what was going on behind the buildings of the front line opposite from you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We couldn't see that. How could we see behind the buildings? We can't see through the buildings. How could we see what was going on behind those building?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you told us that attacks were a daily occurrence by the BH army against Nedzarici, can you describe to us up to the moment when you were wounded, what did buildings look like on your side and on their side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On our side right in the very early days of the war buildings, our homes started to burn, but that was because of the gunfire. And those buildings which were in front of us were also burning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, in the course of this case we have had the opportunity to see the maps of lines which are marked and which the Prosecution handed over to Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence would like to show the witness a map marked 3278. It is a set of 26 maps covering individual incidents explaining to us by Mr. Karavelic. Specifically on one of these maps, we are dealing with the incident 26, and we can see a part of Nedzarici. And I would like, of course, with your leave, the witness to be shown this map. And in view of his soldier in that part of the -- of the area, I would like him to tell us and to show us the line which is drawn here was the real line, that is, may the witness do it with your leave? I have copied --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Since the witness is not allowed to mark on this map, Madam Usher, could you make sure that there are no pens around. This is just a map to look at and not to make any markings, Mr. DP6.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have copied it, though -- I mean, it is black and white. With your leave, perhaps the witness, DP6, if he thinks that this map is not, then perhaps we can give him the black and white map. And then he draw on it and show us where the line was, but we shall wait.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If any marking is needed, then it could be done on the copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, on the map before you, can you simply show us the line that you drew on the map? Do we see this line drawn here? Will you merely show to us the line, the front line of the two sides, the front lines of the two sides. Let me help you. The green line indicates the positions of the army of Republika Srpska. And the light green or blue, if I may put it that way, indicates the positions of the BH army. Can you now tell us if these positions as they are drawn here reflect the situation whilst you were at that front line --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object. That is not the evidence. The evidence of the witness was that the lines were incorrectly placed and he then corrected it with the marker which appears on the map. And as I understand my learned colleague's question, she confines herself to the dark green line and the light green line. The appropriate line is the black one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, my next question is: Between these two lines, the green and light green, do you see where your front line was? Do you see another line there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These lines, these green and light green, they are not drawn here. Because they both go into Nedzarici, that is our positions. And this is the Lukavicka Cesta the Lukavicka Road. And these here are buildings that they occupied. This is the shopping centre and these are the buildings where they were. These buildings here, this is the shopping centre and then we have the health centre here and then this locality there with the houses. And the light green line, it goes through Nedzarici, but they were not here. They were beyond that line, that is -- that is in the shopping centre. These buildings here and then on, as I have already explained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DP6, between this light green and the dark green lines -- no, don't make any markings. But do you see any other lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I see this blue line here, but this one is -- this is a wrong line and this is inaccurate too because it is not true. The Muslim troops were on this side of the street as, I have already said. In this area here. So this line is not correct; it is not true that they were here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, it has both become clear that the early markings, as from the answers of the witness now, that the troops he belonged to were on the one side of the road in little houses and that the BH forces were at the other side of the road in high-rise buildings. So would you please continue then. I mean, it is now for the second or the third time that we hear the same evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, between the blue line and the dark green line, you can see buildings drawn. In that part which is framed by the blue and the green colour, do these buildings exist and what are these buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These buildings between the dark green and blue line, they do not exist. Here is a centre, I mean the professional -- the centre for the professional rehabilitation of blind and disabled persons. So the other side is the Aleja Branko Bujica liar, and the other side is the blind children's home. That was a primary school. And on this side here, these are no buildings. I don't know what this is. Because these buildings did not exist on our side except the home for the blind and the blind children institute. This is crossing into our territory. There were no buildings. They were merely the old people's home and the home for the blind. But as they drew this, this part here probably, it looks as if this one is the blind people's home and this one the old people's home. I don't understand what this is. Because these buildings, they were -- these buildings here, they were in these high-rise buildings and the shopping centre. And here the health centre is not marked and the houses that were here where the Muslim soldiers were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, on this map, you just told us that this map did not reflect the real-life situations. You told us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Firstly, I note that none of this was put to General Karavelic as it should have been done in cross-examination. But secondly, having regard to the transcript of the witness's last answer, it will be impossible to determine from it any sense because my learned colleague in her next question, has not sought to clarify for the transcript what he was pointing to. I am wondering, Mr. President, if it should be done or if he can live without that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this map, the map that the witness is looking at now, the witness looked at a few days ago. And at the time when Mr. Karavelic was testifying about this map, the Defence was not aware of the real-life situation on the site. And that is why I am showing this map to Witness DP6 because he was there throughout. And we think that he is a person fully qualified to describe to us the positions and the distribution of buildings in this part of the locality. And that is why the Defence could not ask Mr. Karavelic about the map and the positions and could only ask this witness who was there. I couldn't show this map to the witness earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Just for the record, essentially, the Prosecution does not accept that. The maps were provided to the Defence in advance throughout the eight months of the Prosecution case. And in particular, from the second and third months, there was much evidence as to where the front line was in this critical area. The Defence had every opportunity to obtain its instructions from its client and from others as to where they say the front line was. But I don't seek to push that any further at this stage. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that is a slight difference, and the maps are not the same either. Because on one map, streets are without any width, where on the other map the streets have some -- these are maps that deal with the same area but are not drawn specifically the same in respect of streets, buildings, et cetera. So it is -- it might be a bit difficult to compare them. But, Ms. Pilipovic I have been listening now for quite some time and so has the Chamber. We heard a lot of evidence now. Could you please come to your point.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The last evidence we heard was that the buildings on the map marked by Witness Karavelic shows buildings that do not exist. On the other map you just gave to the witness, there seem to be at least there are dark red buildings just next to that same street, the Lukavicka Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Cesta as well. So I am still a bit confused. The testimony of this witness is clear that these buildings indicated on this map do not exist, and the front line is wrong to the extent that it was one side of the street and the other side of the street, rather than, as it is indicated here, both front lines just west of the street. So, would you please continue and come to your point.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. All I wish to say is that Mr. Karavelic was heard in July, and that he was the one who drew these lines. So the Defence could not know whether Mr. Karavelic would be confirming this or not in his testimony, confirming the accuracy of this during his testimony. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, on this map, do you see two small circles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One has "26" and the other one has "25."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, from the line which you hold, so to speak, can you see these marked places? Are they in your field of vision? Can you tell us, can you see these marked places?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean from our position?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And can you tell us which street it is? Do you know what part is in this locality and what is this locality called?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Alipasino Polje number 26 and 25. And the 25 -- 25 it's up there, its the intersection. And this is Alipasino Polje. It is right behind Vojnicko Polje. Behind these buildings, there is an intersection which separates the Alipasino end. But it is an intersection because this is a street, a road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, can you tell us which street is it the "25" -- where "25" is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I have forgotten what it is called, but it will come to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that intersection and this street, can you see them from your positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We couldn't see either the intersection or the street. Why? Because at number 25, there were containers and screens. So there was no way you could see that street from our positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am looking at the clock. I believe it is time for us to have a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Pilipovic. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, either at this stage or when we resume, might I have a minute to address the Chamber in the absence of the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will adjourn until 11.00. And, Madam Usher, would you not bring in the witness before we enter the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, you wanted to address the Chamber in the absence of the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Firstly, in relation to the French letter. We haven't yet receive a translation. We have asked the translation unit to give us a draft translation as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We will deal with that then after --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the reason I wish to address you relates to the last few questions asked by the Defence -- excuse me, Ms. Pilipovic has asked the witness effectively whether the crime scene for scheduled sniping incident 25 could be viewed from positions held by the SRK. She has not yet asked the witness specifically what the situation was as of the date of the incident. But I think I can reasonably assume that she would not have led this evidence if she does not intend ultimately to establish that the response applied to the date in question. Essentially, the answer is that the crime scene could not be seen from SRK positions because, "there were containers and screens." Mr. President, this again raises the issue of the failure by the Defence to have put relevant aspects of the Defence case to the appropriate Prosecution witnesses, as they are required to do by the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. I raised this issue I think last week in a core sense and pointed out the various possible outcomes which flow from this fundamental failure. This one is particularly serious. The one in relation to the map is not of critical importance, far from it, but this is. Essentially, the witness, the eyewitness, gave evidence that she lived in the apartment block adjacent to where the shooting took place. And she could easily have been asked, and indeed it could easily have been put to her, that it was impossible to see the other side of the confrontation line from where her friend was shot, since this witness was immediately alongside her friend when she was shot. Mr. President, I don't propose to make these submissions every time Defence demonstrates such a failure, and that is why I sought to say these words in the absence of the witness. Ultimately, it is a matter for the transcript. The transcript, when studied, will demonstrate where witnesses have not -- Prosecution witnesses have not been confronted according to the Rules. It is not, in my respectful submission, sufficient for the Defence to shrug its shoulders and say, well, we were only informed of this in the last few days; not for matters like this. This is an incident which was scheduled to the indictment. The Defence had ample time to make their inquiries, and specifically if, as it now seems, their case is that the crime scene could not have been viewed from SRK positions, then surely that is something which they, either were aware of or should have been aware of at the time that the crime-based witness was called by the Prosecution. So, Mr. President, I make the objections in these full terms now and emphasise that I will not -- I do not propose to do so as a matter of course from this point on. And I remind you that ultimately it may well lead to the Prosecution seeking leave to either recall a large number of witnesses so that these matters can be put, alternatively, for inferences to be drawn against the Defence where they have not fulfilled their obligation under the Rules under Procedure and Evidence. Mr. President -- excuse me for a moment. I may have one other comment to make in relation to this issue, if I could be allowed to do so, perhaps at the end of the next break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you to respond, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was trying to follow carefully what my learned colleague said. I don't know whether I will be able to follow though transcript. If it is necessary, my co-counsel could perhaps help me with this. But I have to say that throughout the time that the witnesses of the Prosecution were heard, the Defence always asked the questions or cross-examined, depending on the examination-in-chief. Specifically, we can talk about the incident 25. Here we heard the witness. We know from the statement of the witness that she said from which direction the firing came. And then at all the questions asked by the Defence, when we are talking about the Prosecution witnesses, were directed in a sense asking: "In the vicinity where you lived and where you were, were there military, were there military targets?" Mostly or generally all of the witnesses of the Prosecution said there was no army, there were no troops, no military targets, they were either walking by, they were passing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, I think that the objection of Mr. Ierace was about your questions in relation to containers or whatever would take the view from potential perpetrators of the incident from the scene of the crime. I think that is what his objection was about, and that you have not put that to these witnesses. For example, let me just try to understand what the Prosecution says, is that you did not put to a witness -- I just have to be careful that she is not protected.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, we are making some inquiries about that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least the victim that was shot?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: She was not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is Medina Omerovic, that you did never put to her whether there was anything that would take the sight from where she was, looking at that spot from the other side of the confrontation line. I think that is what essentially is what the objection of Mr. Ierace is about. And he says, then we would have to -- if this is part of the Defence case, then you should have put that to this witness, and otherwise, we might be in a position that we have to recall that witness. And what we heard from you until now is that you said we were only aware of this fact since last week. And Mr. Ierace says to the Chamber that that is not a sufficient response and that the Defence should have prepared their case in an earlier stage, since it has been an incident which was scheduled long ago. From your answer, I have some difficulties in relating your answer to the objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence can stress here, but it will be necessary for me to analyse the transcript as well. But certainly, the questions of the Defence were always directed in this direction in a sense, did she go? Where did she go? What did she see? Were there troops there? Was there protection? I am now in a position to go back in time and recall everything about every single incident and what every witness said. Now, certainly Defence tried to ask these questions of every witness. So the Defence that my learned colleague -- the attitude of my learned colleague, the position of my learned colleague is certainly not the correct one. I asked this witness specifically about this point. I didn't ask about the incident or anything. I asked which street this was. And the witness explained this area here, and where the two armies were, and the area where the buildings were, as he said, completely covered the area that was under the control of the army of Republika Srpska. I did not speak to him about the incident. I only asked him about which street that was and whether this street could be viewed from the positions of the army of Republika Srpska. I think that was my question. I cannot go back in the transcript. I will, if you allow me, I will just confirm it with my colleague for a few moments about the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps then may I ask the following: Also in view of the pre-trial Defence brief and also in view of the submissions made during the last month, in respect of -- I take it, that we are now talking about incident 25 or 26. What exactly is the case of the Defence? That place where the victims were could not be seen from the other side of the confrontation line or that they could not be seen by this witness from where he was working, or what is the Defence case in this respect?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Specifically talking, Your Honour, when we are talking about incident number 5 -- 25, first of all, we spoke about the demarcation lines. And the Defence's case is that on both sides there were soldiers on the front lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just first ask --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The second --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...part. Is it contested by the Prosecution that there were soldiers on both sides of the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What -- please continue, Ms. Pilipovic. So that is the first part, not contested.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The second part of the Defence's position is that alongside demarcation lines, positions of both armies, there were daily clashes between the armies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that contested, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is not contested. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another part of the position of the Defence is that if we bear in mind the distance between these two demarcation lines, that is, if there were army firing in the vicinity, the Defence's case is that this was on a daily basis. And there were daily attacks by BH army, particularly when we are talking about this position and the height of these buildings, and the view that all of the soldiers of the BH army were able to see from these positions in relation to the positions of the Republika Srpska army. So if we agreed that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I stop you on this point. So the third point is that the positions in high-rise buildings gave the BiH soldiers a, may I say, an excellent view on the other side of the confrontation line which would have allowed them to attack from that position. Is that contested?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Specifically, when we are talking about this incident here we know and our position is and this was done during the examination-in-chief -- cross-exam of Medina Omerovic that she had been warned -- she had been warned that the soldiers were present on the third floor of the building. They were in uniform and they told her that she shouldn't be going there because there was firing. At that time, she said there was firing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that contested?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the Defence doesn't know and is unable to find out whether this was so, but if this was so, as the witness Medina Omerovic stated during her testimony, and the matter was the wounding of her friend Sanela Muratovic and if this did happen. And again the Defence doesn't know if this did take place. Now, if she had been wounded, this could have only happened by chance because there was an exchange of fire of both sides because of the soldiers who were present on both sides. So if it did happen, it came by chance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is the conclusion you draw from these --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, what our position is, what the position of the Defence is, is that if there were daily shooting, and if the BH army fired from better positions, if there was -- if there was wounding at all, this could have only happened by accident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand. We went through the four factual issues: Presence of soldiers, daily clashes, the position of the BiH, and the warning to the victim. And you say we draw some inferences from that and that is the position of the Defence. My problem is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- I am sorry. This is not quite the position of the Defence. The Defence will tell you about its position as soon as the co-counsel can have a French transcript, French interpretation of the French -- the transcript of the French interpretation which will happen in the few days, as I am having difficulties in the interpretation and I cannot explain now certain things to Ms. Pilipovic. I will be able to give you some information, if you allow me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We did spend a lot of time to establish the presence of soldiers. We did spend a lot of time on daily exchange of fire. We did spend a lot of time on who was in high-rise buildings and who was not. And we did not, until now, of course, and that is not illogical, spend any time on a potential warning of the witness. So we could have -- since it is not contested, it is not the Prosecution's case that there were no soldiers. So I would say all these facts that make you conclude that it should have been by chance that the victim was hit, the underlying facts are not in dispute, as far as I see. So therefore, we would not have had to spend time specifically on that. I would not mind, this Chamber would not mind, as you know, to especially perhaps with the first witnesses, to give a general impression and to say, well, they were in high-rise buildings. So we are not opposing to it. But whether this should take so much time when it is not a contested issue, that is another matter. But is it also the case of the Defence -- and I think that's part of the problem of Mr. Ierace, is it also case of the Defence that the victim was not visible from the other side of the confrontation line because there were -- well, whatever, sheets or -- well, the protection measures as we saw -- heard of them in many testimonies, containers. So, in order to protect people passing by from fire. Is that also the case of the Defence? I mean, that is different from -- if you say it is by chance, that is different from saying you could not have been hit because there was no view to target. I mean, that is how I understand if there are any -- I mean, is that the case of the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, bearing in mind specifically this incident, the position of the Defence is that these buildings which were on the side, on our side, we completely rule out that this incident, if it did take place at all if the wounded had taken place, could not have happened from the positions under the control of the Republika Srpska army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And for --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We do not know whether this person was wounded at all, and how this happened at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But is it part of the case of the Defence that because of the presence of such, I would say, visual barriers, the witness -- the victim could not have been hit from positions held by the -- by the Serbian forces. That is part of the Defence case as well. Now the question raised by Mr. Ierace is -- I do not remember, but perhaps you could refresh my memory -- that it is somewhere -- is it in your pre-trial brief of the Defence or is it -- where could I have read this that this, and perhaps specifically in view of this incident. I don't know whether you are referring to 25 and 26 or just to the victim Sanela Muratovic because we have dealt with both 25 and 26. Where do I find that this is part of the Defence case?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, at this moment I would have to look and in our pre-trial brief as I was preparing for this witness, and I should look at the transcript. As far as Medina Omerovic, I think that was in March 2002, but I cannot give you exact analysis now about the position of the Defence. I apologise. I am not sure whether the gentleman Dzunko -- Mr. Dzunko was protected or not because I did mention his name. But this is a specific question that the Chamber has for the Defence. But at this very moment, I would have to focus on the precise way this position was explained. I believe that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that as far as the other victim is concerned, that there would be no confusion as to whether there were any visual barriers or not. I think there were. That's the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if my memory serves me well, incident 26 has to do with sitting in a room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It is clear that the obstruction -- especially from a distance, the obstruction of view is clear in the Defence case, I think. So the issue is about Sanela Muratovic. Whether the Defence has claimed in any of its submissions that because of the obstruction of view from the Serbian-held positions, that she could not have been targeted from there. I mean, that is the issue that Mr. Ierace raises, that he is surprised to hear it now, that it has not been put to the witness which would have been Medina Omerovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that such a question was asked. I am trying to think back. But I will check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You will have to check that. Because if that is true, the objection of Mr. Ierace would be without merit. And the Chamber should then make this clear. So therefore, we will check that. Another issue is to use our time as efficient as possible, perhaps since we really didn't spend a lot of time on issues of which it is now -- it has now become clear that it is not contested in whatever way, it is not part of the Prosecution case that there were no soldiers on both of the confrontation lines, so there were no frequent clashes. So we can just accept that then. And if there is any doubt, please ask the Prosecution. And I am certain if it is not contested, that the Prosecution will allow you to if you want to repeat that to establish that by leading questions, is it true that there were soldiers on both sides of the confrontation lines and was there frequent fighting. That makes one minute. Then you make your point, you put your argument in place, and we would not have to spend so much time on it. That's one of the issues I would like to bring to your attention. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, concretely -- thank you, Your Honour. As far as I can analyse the victim incident -- victims so far, I believe it was the only victim who was heard and who said that it was on the third floor, if I am correct, that there were a couple of soldiers who warned her not to go where she was headed because there was shooting there. I think it was the only incident. But in any event, an analysis -- we shall analyse every incident. If we need to cut the time shorter, we shall analyse every incident individually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, only to finish this and move on, I want to say one thing. In order to save time the Defence worked last night very late in order to prepare reasons -- to give you the reasons and I do not think -- I think that this is becoming a very, very serious matter now. Mr. President, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just a quick response and then we will move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, very quick. I hope this will ultimately save a lot of time. There is another aspect of this incident which, I think, demonstrates a fundamental and serious concern. We did receive an amplified "summary of facts" as to which the witness will testify, that is, this particular witness. And we received that on the 13th of October, 2002. It is a paragraph long, approximately 20 lines. The only reference to this aspect is as follows: "He will speak about facts important for scheduled sniping incidents numbers 18, 21, 25, and 26." It is wholly inadequate. We have no idea what this witness will say about incidents 18, 21 and 26. We have heard a little about 25. In my respectful submission, that does not meet on the part of the Defence their responsibilities under the Rules. It is not a summary of the facts about which he will testify. This should have been included. If I may, Mr. President, and I say this only because I don't intend to rise to my feet on every occasion, to the extent that it might be thought or suggested that the problem confronted by the Defence is explicable in terms of their legal culture, I have done a little study of comparative criminal procedure. And it is clear to me that in the civil law system where there is an investigating magistrate, in a situation such as this the eyewitnesses would be confronted, would have put to them, the account put by the Defence, that is, the person who determines the facts. He is assisted by knowing what the response is of the relevant witnesses to contention put by the other side. That is how it is done in the civil law system; this is how it is done in the common law system. Both ways lead to the result, that the fact finder is assisted by knowing what the response would be. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, whether your analysis of the civil law system is acceptable to the Chamber, we will still have to consider that. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. In any legal system, in any legal system, if a problem arises, one takes a telephone, one calls and says, what is this? Mr. Ierace received on the 13th this information. If he did not understand, if he did not know, if he couldn't imagine, if he couldn't anticipate whatever about the firing conditions, he could have well called us and asked us, Did you discuss the possibilities of this and this? And then we would have a dialogue. It is not really right to wait for the last moment to waste I don't know how much time. That is perhaps so, but we did not understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems to be an important aspect of the testimony. I think it should have been provided by the Defence. And the vague wordings could have given the Prosecution a reason to ask for further explanation. We will now ask Madam Usher to bring the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated, Mr. DP6. Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6 --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like again the witness to be shown the map with incident 26.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, you have in front of you the map that you looked at before the break, in relation to the lines and buildings about which you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. told us that they did not exist. On the right-hand side, can you identify the three structures in the upper corner. You said it was Vojnicko Polje. Above number 25, you said that it was Aleja Branka Bujic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Aleja Branka Bujica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far does it extend?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Aleja Branka Bujica goes straight down to the terminal -- no, up to here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us above the three buildings which are drawn.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which ones?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Above the line that you tell us is Aleja Branka Bujica. Above the Aleja Branka Bujica.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. Above. Where you have three red dots. See, as if in a triangle, two buildings above the buildings in the upper corner.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, will you tell us what is the street which is an extension of Aleja Branka Bujica, as you tell us, to the three red dots, towards number 13 and 2 where it says.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Now I understand what you mean. Aleja Branka Bujica extends as far as this place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then what follows?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What then goes towards the tram terminal in Nedzarici. I am not quite sure what the street is called.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us these two structures which you have there, what are these?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean these ones? These are student hostels.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, can you tell us, until October of 1993 and as of October 1993 do you have any direct knowledge whether in these structures there were any troops?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whose?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the transcript, the witness, above -- no, below number 2 and 13, the witness is pointing at two buildings, two structures, and he tells us that these are students hostels.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, the witness is pointing to two triangular at least tripod I would have to say structures left from the numbers 2 and 13.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. DP6, you are telling us that in these students hostels there was the BH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP, while you were in your locality and during the conflict, can you tell us if there were any UNPROFOR forces there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: UNPROFOR came to the students hostels from time to time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us when was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can give you -- I can't give you the dates. I can give you approximately times. They were there, I think, in August or September. But they kept coming there except -- but they were not quartered in those students hostels, but they did visit the students hostels in front of students hostels.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us why did they go there? Do you have any knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know why. But when they were there then there would be no fire coming from the students hostels.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you personally have any contact with UNPROFOR representatives?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, can you tell us about the time when you were there, that is until February 1993, you told us that you commanded a company. Who was the battalion commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radivoje Grkovic commanded the battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, was he your commander for the duration while you were in Nedzarici -- I'm sorry, I mentioned a place.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until February 1993, the battalion commander was Radivoje Grkovic

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you returned in October 1993, was Mr. Grkovic still your commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who issued orders to you as the company commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The battalion commander issued orders to me as the company commander. And presumably it was the battalion commander but it was -- the battalion commander received his orders from the brigade commanders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6 how personally as the company commander, how did you report to your superiors? When I say "how," I mean in what way, that is, orally or in writing and how often?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My reports were oral and they went to the battalion command and it was by using the field telephone or at night when darkness would fall, then I would go there if need be and report orally again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you and how receive reports from your subordinates or rather who were your subordinates since you were a company commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Platoon leaders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did platoon leaders report to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Orally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that they reported orally, did they ever -- did your subordinates ever report to you about the situation in the zone of your company? Did they report to you whether there had been any fighting, whether there had been any casualties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they submitted their daily oral reports on that or by field telephone. They reported whether there had been any wounded or killed on our side or anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they also report to you about possible shellings by the BH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they report the positions from which it came?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they reported the shell has arrived from this or that direction, and the shell hit this or that place in our area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you tell us that your superior was the battalion commander, can you tell us what kind of orders did your battalion commander issue? What was the substance of these orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The substance of these orders was roughly not to fire just like that without provocation, that is, naturally if we were attacked we had to return the fire to repel the attack. I mean, the orders of the battalion commander by and large went in that direction, were in that sense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, can you tell us after your -- after October 1993, you had a different battalion commander. What kind of orders were his?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they are more or less the same. The orders were the same as before I returned, before I was wounded. Not to fire just like that, if there was no need to, and if the other side attacked, then we, of course, always had to fire. We had to defend ourselves. And the majority of the orders had to deal with the fact that we were not to fire at civilians, at women, and so on. This was prohibited strictly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, can you tell us how were you issued with ammunition --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. I am very sorry, but I heard the witness say in the language that I am following: "Not only civilians and women, but also children and elderly." These are the two things that he said which are missing from the transcript. And it is the -- it has to do with specific instructions that he received from his superiors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
