utterances.text: Did you refer, apart from civilians and women, also to children and elderly people, that you were ordered not to target? Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, when your subordinates reported to you about the situation in their areas of responsibility, did you ever get a report that somebody had hit a civilian or that some civilians -- that there were some civilian casualties? Did you ever receive such a report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, I said a moment ago that we were forbidden to fire at civilians, the elderly, and children. I said it a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, before I asked you that, I asked you about the supply of provision of ammunition. Can you tell us how and who requested the ammunition and what was the situation regarding the quantities that you had at your disposal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the early days, we had enough ammunition. But later on, perhaps sometime in June, we had to apply for ammunition and in some detail how much we spend, and if so much then why so much, because it was a short supply. One was not to open fire at random during brawls or whatever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, on this map you pointed at students hostels and told us that troops were there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- and if yes, then from which positions were you able to look through the buildings of the student hostels?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can I look through the buildings?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any direct knowledge that these students hostels were on fire? Did they burn?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was that, do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't exactly. It was in the early days of the war, June, July, I really don't know. I can't remember the date. All I know is that they were in flames. One could see the flames.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But could you use them, that is, could they be used if they had burned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because the walls remained standing as walls. Those hostels were not demolished. There were still walls standing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, on this map, can you point at the Oslobodjenje building? Do you see it here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the Oslobodjenje building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us -- can you tell us about this Oslobodjenje building? Was it used by some army and which?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was used by the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say, "it was used," when? At what time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout the war, while I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge whether there were any troops there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the troops were there, just like the student hostels. So these are big buildings, and they used those big buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, can you tell us in the area that you lived in, which was the tallest building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tallest building was the monastery, that is the faculty of theology.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge that whether during the conflict that is in 1992, 1993, 1994, until August, whether there were any troops in that area and whether troops used that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, troops used that building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that it was the tallest building, can you tell us how many storeys?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four. Four floors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, in view of your of your testimony, can you tell us and your stay in that locality, can you tell us whether you had electricity and water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the locality, there was no electricity. And when there is no electricity, then there is no water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us at which time intervals were you left without water and electricity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1992 until I was there until 1993, there was no electricity at all. And when there was no electricity, there was no water either. So we use water because there was some old wells which were used ages before that. And we cleaned them up and put lime in them to disinfect them and that was the water that we used for washing, for laundry, and the rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, can you tell us, because we heard a number of testimonies about an Institute for the Blind.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point on the map at this institute.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The institute for blind children is located vis-a-vis the Aleja Branka Bujica. It should be around here somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the transcript, Mr. DP6 is explaining that between the blue and the dark green line, the first rectangle that we can see, and to the north is the building of the Institute for the Blind.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Institute for Blind Children.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Institute for Blind Children. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just try to be a bit more precise.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the street called Branka Bujica, Aleja Branka Bujica Street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to be very precise. I see on the map a number "13"; that's where the blue line appears between the dark and the softer green line. There appears number "13." And I noticed that the witness pointed at a rectangular which is the fourth of a row of four from north-west to south-east, closest to crossroads, and that is a crossroad that appears between numbers 13 and two larger constructions at the other side of the crossroad close to number 25. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, when you indicated to the building, you said it was Institute for Blind Children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the area of your locality, were there other such institutes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a centre for the blind and the disabled. These were plants, production plants. This is where people who worked who had graduated from schools and who had vocational degrees, they were able to work in this production.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. DP6. I just want to ask if you can tell us, this institute, as you called it Centre for the Blind, could you tell us where that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was located approximately here where you can see the small square, on the other side from the Bujca Aleja very near to the Lukavicka Cesta, about here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. DP6. Mr. DP6, when you spoke about the Institute for Blind Children, can you tell us, do you know who was using this facility during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we perhaps locate a bit more precise where the Institute for the Blind Children was at one side of the road in a -- the lowest in a -- I think it is a red rectangular shape, just opposite the road between the dark green line and the blue line. The first structure in south-easterly direction was pointed at by the witness, which has a rectangular shape in the main direction of that structure going from south-west to north-east, just opposite the two bigger structures I mentioned before. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, when you spoke about the Institute for Blind Children, I asked you if you knew whether this facility was operational and who was using it in 1992, 1993, 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This facility was used by the army of Republika Srpska from 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally visit this facility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Considering that you did visit the facility, could you tell us perhaps in relation to the view towards the triangular buildings which are the student hostels, could you tell us what was your view like in relation to the street which is parallel to the student hostels?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In relation to this street here?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. In relation to this street parallel to the student hostels. First of all, could you tell us the distance, in your opinion, approximately.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 400 metres, perhaps 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the view?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe there is more than 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your view, if you are at the Institute for the Blind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean looking at the street?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Were you able to see what was going on in the street with the view through the student hostel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can't see through the student hostel because these are buildings where you have walls. It is impossible to see. Moreover, it is all black because they had burnt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- from the Institute for Blind Children that you say was used by the army of Republika Srpska and you say that you visited there, could you tell us how tall was that building? How many storeys did it have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think about 15, 20 floors, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am talking about the Institute for the Blind.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, Institute for the Blind, yes. It had two floors. It has two floors, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us on which floor was the army or was the whole building used by the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army was on the first floor; it was on the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter lost part of the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just ask you to repeat your answer. You said, "I think the army was on the ground floor," that is what you said, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It was on the ground floor and occasionally it would go to the first floor, upstairs, the first floor was like an observation point. And on the first floor, you couldn't set guards there because of security. And it was on the ground floor that we made these trenches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, could you tell us how often did you go to the Institute for the Blind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go that often. Perhaps once a week, once a fortnight I would go just for some consultations or for some discussions. Because it was impossible to cross to this to -- cross over the street to get to that building. You had to go all the way around. You had to go to the barracks and then go through the buildings where there were screens in order to get -- and then you cross the trenches and then you get to the Institute for the Blind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I apologise. I believe that what I heard -- no, it is in the transcript. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, I didn't understand you correctly. Where was it impossible to cross from? When I asked you how frequently you went --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was impossible to go from Lukavicka Cesta across the Aleja Branka Bujica to the Institute for the Blind. But you had to go all the way around to the barracks and then from the barracks you would go by the buildings --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you think that you could show it to us on the map? Where did you go from the positions of the Lukavicka Cesta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately -- this map is no good. But I will show you, approximately. I approximately went through here -- from here to here and then here. Here is the barracks here. And then you went to this part. And here there was some private houses, so you went alongside these private houses. Here there was a kind of opening. There was a trench there. Through the trench and then you would get to the Institute for Blind Children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you didn't dare go --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, we don't have a record of that. Might I suggest that perhaps we use the other map and mark it to show the route and we clarify where the starting point is, what the significance of the starting point is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It is also important how precise the route is. What the witness indicated is that he would not cross the street, but go first in south-westerly direction on the scale of this map, approximately 3 to 400 metres, then go to the other side of the road, and then to move in north-westerly -- northeasterly direction, again to reach the Institute of the Blind Children. If there is need for any more precision, I would like you to ask the witness to mark it; if not, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. No, Your Honour, there is no need for that. Just that -- although, I do have a map. I have a map which is black and white, and if it is necessary, we can mark it in. But considering your explanation, I don't think it is necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you have to use that route, Mr. DP6?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had to use this route because there was firing, there was shooting. It was visible. You couldn't cross from Lukavicka Cesta to the Institute for the Blind to get directly across the road; you had to go all the way around. Because the army had made the route for itself and then you would get to the Institute for Blind Children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know personally how frequent -- how frequent was that considering that you went frequently?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean? What happened frequently?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How frequently were these positions targeted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was targeted on a daily basis. Because not a day went by without shooting here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let me just confer a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my colleague has a few questions and then we will finish. I believe that we are within the time frame that the Defence has.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time would you approximately need, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Five minutes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is the following: From what you call the Institute for the Blind, were you able to - yes or no - see the street, the road which was on the other side of the two triangular buildings that you call the student hostel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the Institute for Blind Children, you were able to see; while the centre for professional rehabilitation, you were not. So you were able to see from the building next to the Aleja Branka Bujica, you were able to see; while from the Lukavicka Cesta, you were not able to see the student hostels, you could just see the top floors, maybe the top two floors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But my question was the following: Were you able to see the street which was behind these two buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. My second question is the following: Witness, do you know if the neighbourhood or the locality of Nedzarici was targeted by shelling by the other side, by the opposing side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, if this was the case, what could you say about the intensity of the shellings on one hand, and of the results in terms of destruction, particularly destruction of buildings and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nedzarici was shelled occasionally. For instance, I remember on one occasion, I think it was in June, perhaps between 15th and 20th of June - I can't tell you the date exactly - when a shell hit the old people's home. On that occasion, six old elderly people were killed that we were not able to take out immediately. We couldn't take their bodies out immediately, but we had to wait for the night. And it was only after that that we managed to get them out. So that was the first time when really a lot of people were killed by a shell. In that old people's home were elderly people of all three ethnic backgrounds, Muslims, Croats and Serbs. And the same thing happened in July, there was another shell that hit the old people's home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I will let you see two photographs and they have numbers. D1761, and D1762, and to start with I would like you to tell us if you can Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. identify them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would just like to specify that these photographs where there is also a copy for the Prosecution, they were properly disclosed at the time and -- but of course the Defence has got a copy for everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just to clarify this, I don't think we received any warning of either number. We have received one of the photographs, the other one we are seeing for the first time. So if my friend could try and keep the proposed exhibit list up to date. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The two proposed photographs have been disclosed at the relevant time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, could you please have a look at the photographs that you were handed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we could have them put on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the assistance of the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...on the ELMO, Madam Usher, once the witness had a look at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Since you put that one on the ELMO, we will have a look at this second photograph ending with a "two" in this number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please tell us if this photograph corresponds to a neighbourhood that you know, the photograph which is now on the ELMO, please. Specifically, is this an area -- is this Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Witness, if we assume, and I know it is -- this was taken very recently, that is, only a few months ago, is the state of the destruction at the time which happened in this neighbourhood is comparable, similar, or different from what we see on the photograph today?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President, for a number of reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Firstly, what time is the question directed to; secondly, and more importantly again, relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If we are talking about relevance, it sometimes it useful to ask the witness to take off his headphones. May I first ask you, Mr. DP6, do you understand any French or English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please take off your headphones for a second. Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. The question of relevance is the following: We have here buildings, it seems to me, obviously civilian buildings and the witness just told us that this is a neighbourhood of Sarajevo. Now, what we would want to show is that there were firing errors and buildings could be destroyed certainly by shellings and certainly by firing errors. If these firing errors were numerous in the area of Nedzarici, and if this witness tells us, yes, there were shells which exploded very frequently and very frequently buildings were destroyed as a direct consequence, then it seems very useful for us to say that on both sides this was the case. And I believe that this is a very important evidence in terms of reasonable doubt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am trying to follow you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. How can we see from this photograph where we see heavily damaged buildings that have a civilian appearance, how can we see that they were not intentionally shelled? Because you indicate to us that the relevance is that if such errors could occur in Nedzarici, they could have occurred at the other side as well. I do not know how you can see that from a photograph, but if you could please then -- and whether the witness would know that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I am just responding to your concern. If what I presume the witness will say, he will say that all of the buildings were in this state. So there were only two hypothesis. One side -- on one side, there is only deliberate shooting, and if this -- I am saying this is not a good hypothesis. And the second hypothesis, there was a very high degree of firing errors. And this is what we want to show in dispute. I don't think that there is another possibility except intentional, deliberate, and errors. Because of a number of buildings that were hit, we believe that this was a very high degree of errors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So what you want to establish of the relevance is that there was an extensive damage of buildings, and then the next part is how you would explain that. Is that in dispute that there was extensive damage done to buildings in the Nedzarici area, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Not as termed, Mr. President, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that is not in dispute. And I think the second part, unless there is some specific reason to assume that the witness could explain to us whether this was the result of deliberate targeting, buildings of a civilian appearance, or that if these were errors. If you have reason to believe so, you may proceed; if it is just to establish the extensive damaging of these houses, I think these pictures where the witness testified where it was Nedzarici could support that and we could look at it and it could be admissible in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, just to make things simple and since we have this witness who knew the area, and since we say, if I understand it correctly, we say there was extensive damage, as you put it, may I ask a direct question to the witness, put it directly, whether he knew about firing mistakes, firing errors, during shellings and were they occurring in Nedzarici directly? We would gain -- save time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me -- I think the first question you should then put to the witness is whether he has any specific knowledge of targeting of shells fired by the opposite armed forces. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you want to put questions to the witness, I will first ask him to put his earphones on again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you have any knowledge, personal knowledge, of the fact and perhaps of the means used by Muslim forces to conduct, carry out, shellings on Nedzarici? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did they use weapons and in order to find out, did they use weapons like a mortar, for instance? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, did you know whether these weapons used in Nedzarici may have produced, may have resulted, in firing errors, that is, collateral damage? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I have some problems with this question. Would you -- whether that could occur is a rather theoretical question. Could you please ask the witness for facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, directly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if when Muslim forces fired it occasionally happened that there were firing errors? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I understood your invitation to the Defence in proposing this question is that it should include the concept of specific knowledge, and this is an invitation for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me do the following: I know, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, what is the issue you would like to raise. Let me ask the witness because there were some leading elements in it as well. You have seen this picture, Mr. DP6, in front of you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether the shelling that caused this damage to these buildings was targeted against these buildings or that it was because of errors in firing that these buildings were damaged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was shelled. This was burnt. There were no -- these were no mistakes. These buildings were burnt, they were shelled by the Muslim forces. That's that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me ask you in a more general --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These buildings were the ones that burnt the most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There are just two or three buildings with a civilian appearance on this picture. In more general terms, were houses which you would consider to be civilian houses could be hit by shells, do you know whether these civilian houses were targeted as such or that they were hit by shells where other perhaps non-civilian buildings were the targets and, therefore, these civilian buildings would have suffered from firing errors?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know whether they were targeted. I just know that they were hit and they were burnt. Whether they were targeted deliberately to hit this building or house, I really don't know. This is probably known by the person who target -- who did this, who fired, who targeted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Simply, Witness, with your knowledge of the weapons, could you tell me if when a shell is launched there is practically a possibility of error? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object. The witness has said that his area of expertise is anti-aircraft artillery. There has been no suggestion so far that this witness has any expertise or experience in the area of mortar fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from that, the question was in a very general way. Is it in dispute that firing errors can occur?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It is not, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please move to your next subject, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Since this is not in dispute --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that perhaps -- no. Since this is not disputed, thank you. You said that these houses were set on fire, were burnt. Could you tell us, how do you know that and how, with which technical means, were these houses set on fire?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President. For all of the questioning on this topic for the last 15 minutes, my learned colleague has not yet asked when this occurred, and that, of course, is fundamental to relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you, looking at these photographs of these buildings, did you witness when they were hit by shells? Have you seen that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To tell you the truth, I don't know exactly the moment when they were hit. But all of these buildings were destroyed, burnt, and shelled in the first year of the war. The very first year of the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was whether you were present when specifically these buildings were hit by shells?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know exactly if I was there at the time, at that moment, but I know when houses, buildings were burning in Nedzarici. Because when a shell lands on a house, after a few minutes, the house starts burning, and it is burning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And they -- they launched some cocktails, I don't know what they were called, when you throw this cocktail. And then after the shell is launched, then this kind of cocktail with fluid inside would go on the roof and seep down and it would make it more flammable and would make it burn more quickly, the houses burn more quickly then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so you explained to us that there are specific shells that would make the buildings to be on fire easily, and at the same -- and another thing, that is in general, but specifically on these buildings you have no knowledge or?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What do you mean? I have no knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about these buildings being hit by a shell, not being present when that happened.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, probably shells landed there, since they burnt this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand that you recognise these buildings as damaged in such a way that they would have been hit by shells. But you were not present when these specific buildings were hit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't right there at the time when these first two buildings, these two there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is a clear answer. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you indicated that you would need five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, perhaps, I would like to continue, Mr. President. When I say "five minutes" that is always without the objections, but now I will double my estimate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, just two more questions, you spoke about means, incendiary means, that is what you said, and you spoke about the beginning of the war. On the basis of what you said, do you know if this destruction occurred in the first months of the combat or when?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will rephrase.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me, please, when did this destruction take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This destruction --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this an objection on the answer? Then it is an objection on the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, you carefully --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, would you please calm down a bit. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I object to the question for this reason: That the witness has already been closely questioned in appropriate terms to establish his state of knowledge as to when these events occurred. And my learned colleague now seeks to revisit that area, which is something he cannot do in chief. The answer has been clearly given and that is the end of the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There is, however, one problem, Mr. Ierace, the witness was questioned about it not in chief, but by myself and I might have different points of interest. So I reject the objection. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I am going to ask my question again: When precisely you told us earlier that this was the first year of the war, I believe you said but do you know exactly when most of these buildings, when were these buildings destroyed, most of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most damage and destruction was caused June, end of June, July, August, and until the end of the year, approximately that. By the end of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, do you know -- and if you do know, please tell us how much, how many -- how many people died in your neighbourhood, that is in the locality of Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean military and civilians or --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can make a distinction, yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know approximately that there were casualties in war, about 240 in the village of Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact figure, but that is approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By that, do you mean 240 people out of the population that you said to be approximately how much, how many, how many people -- when we started your examination, how many people lived in Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. I didn't say 24. I said 240.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, there is a problem with interpretation. At the very start of your examination, you gave us the approximate total number of citizens living in Nedzarici. Can you remind us of that number, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was about 1.500 inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's it. Very well. So these two hundred and forty people that you talk about, is that civilian and military put together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both military and civilians about 240 approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will have a break until 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, are there any more questions or -- because I didn't see the other photograph used or am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Mr. President. But merely -- and thank you for reminding me of that. We only wanted to show it to the witness to see whether he recognises the area, but since we covered all the issues with the first photograph I didn't want to waste any more time. But if you want me to do that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just wanted to be sure that I -- that you have put all the questions to the witness you wanted. Mr. Ierace, is the Prosecution ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Might the witness be shown Exhibit D1761, perhaps that could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Cross-examined by Mr. Ierace:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: DP6 --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object, Mr. President. I object. I am sorry, but I have just said that we have covered all the issues with the first of these two photographs, which is, therefore, 62 rather than 61. Then we thought that this document was enough. And we did not produce in evidence the document 1761 that we see on the screen and we did not ask any questions about it. And, therefore, we do not think that the Prosecution can refer to something that we -- to a piece of evidence that we did not produce. This is the reason for my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace. Is my understanding correct that you intend to tender this document in relation to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It depends on the answer to the next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As such, if the Defence does not put any questions in relation to this picture, this should not prevent the Prosecution, to which this picture has been disclosed, to use it, and if they want to, to tender that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One of the reasons why I did not produce it was because Mr. Ierace himself said a few moments ago that this photograph had been submitted in a regular manner. And considering the difficulties -- no. I am just saying, it was said that it was not communicated regularly, and then all of a sudden during the cross-examination when it appears that it was, I think that we are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is totally independent from how it was, whether it was communicated in time or not. That is not an issue that should bar the Prosecution from using these photographs. Let's first listen what the question would be. Mr. Ierace, please proceed. The objection is denied.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. In any event, it was the other photograph that had not been supplied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, in that photograph can you see the Institute for the Blind Children? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please take a blue marker and place a circle -- I withdraw that. Can you please point to the Institute for the Blind Children.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one here, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please take a blue pen and place a circle around that building.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, did I call it its correct title, that is, the Institute for Blind Children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This here too and that one. This is the first one -- the first one right next to the Aleja Branka Bujica, this is the second one, and this is the third one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also referred to the Centre for the Blind and Disabled. Would you please point to if it appears in the photographs the building or buildings which were the Centre for the Blind and Disabled.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is this one building over here, this small one, even though there is an extension, but you can't see it here, but I think it's this one. This is for the blind and disabled, and this is the Institute for Blind Children. And this is the centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, for the sake of the record, indicate where the witness pointed at when he said that other buildings were also --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. I can do it in a series of questions for greater accuracy, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have placed a blue circle around a white building that appears to be a ground floor, plus two levels on top of the ground floor. Is that correct? And I think it is white. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, immediately to the right of that building, do you see another building of a --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two more buildings, one in the middle and that one over there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- on the building in the middle. Thank you. Please hold the pointer on that building.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was that building part of the Institute for Blind Children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We believe the witness said it was because he is not speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer and move your mouth closer to the microphone as you do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, I am sorry. This is not an objection. It is a precision that I request. I do not think that we heard the witness's answer. We think he said it is or something like that. But I would like it repeated aloud so as to avoid any mistakes whatsoever. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, it took you four lines when Mr. Ierace last question was: "Could you please repeat your answer?" That is really not very efficient. Could you please repeat that answer, whether this building you just pointed at was also -- did also belong to the Institute for the Blind Children. That is the building in the middle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, and this one here to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will come to that in a minute. Now, would you please take a blue marker and in the sky immediately above the blue circle that you have already put on the photograph, please write the number "1."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you now please place --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is it -- is this blue? Oh, then the light is different. I am sorry. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Maybe perhaps just clarify that. The pen seems to be Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. blue according to the stop. Yes, it is?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you now please place a blue circle around the second building, that is the one in middle that was part of the same complex.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I see that pen, please. I think that the blue -- it is really different on my screen, but it really is blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the record, the witness has placed a number "2" above the circled middle building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you now please point to the building to the right with your pointer and hold the pointer on the building. Thank you. Was that building also part of the complex of buildings for the Institute for Blind Children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please circle that building and place the number "3" above it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, please look again at the building in the circle numbered "1." In front of that building, that is, between the camera and the building, one can see a red building with a red roof. Would you please point to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Red roof? You mean this one here?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Please point to building number one.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number one, here it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see to the bottom right and just inside the circle is a red roof?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. What was that building before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a private house and it burnt down during the war. This picture was taken later. It was roofless during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it was a privately owned house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me Mr. President. Might the witness be shown -- excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you now point again to the buildings that you were -- that you said may have been part of the complex for the Centre for the Blind and Disabled, that is, where there were production plants. Actually, the ELMO could be adjusted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure that those buildings were part of that centre, or do you have some doubt?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, we can see what appears to be a building with a brownish wall facing the camera and behind it some whiter walls. Do you see that? No to the left where the Centre for the Blind and Disabled is positioned.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now just so we can better understand which buildings were part of that centre. At the moment you have your pointer on the building which appears to have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have lost the image. Could the witness please move the photograph, because a moment ago we couldn't see it on our screens. It was outside the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would you please place your pointer again on the building which has a greyish flat roof.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was that building part of the centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you now please place your pointer on the whitish buildings behind it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those buildings or was that building part of the centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the old people's home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please take your blue pen and circle --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am sorry, but the witness precisely indicated what type of building we were talking about. It was good to have in the transcript the name that he has attributed to it, because it does not appear in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The answer is: "This is the old people's home."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but for the transcript, it would be good to say what it is, because he pointed at it very precisely. Ah, now it is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace asked him to point to the white buildings just behind the first building indicated with the grey flat roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We don't have better lighting on our screen. Could we have the photograph back. If not, then, well, never mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...used in evidence, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. May I urge you not to interrupt unless it really serves a good purpose. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please place a blue circle around the building that was the production plant or Centre for the Blind and Disabled and place a number "4" above it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps the ELMO could be adjusted. All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you have placed the number "4" on an area which appears to be a tree. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can you do it again in the sky area above the circle, place a "4."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. All right, you can put the pen down now and perhaps the ELMO could pan back so that we could see all of the photograph. Now, in the foreground of this photograph we see a large concrete slab which appears to be the roof of a car park. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that there during the war, that concrete slab?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the photograph seems to be taken from the balcony area of a high-rise building, and immediately to the right we can see what appears to be a similar high-rise building. Are you familiar with these two buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is Vojnicko Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you gave that answer, did you point to anything on the photograph? Which is Vojnicko Polje --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We withdraw that question. Go on, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vojnicko Polje is right across the street from Nedzarici, on the other side of Lukavicka Cesta. This is part of Vojnicko Polje. This building next to these garages and this building here is in Vojnicko Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say, "this building here," do you mean the building from which the photograph is taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you now pointed to a building on the right. Thank you. Were these two buildings on the ABiH side of the confrontation lines at the end of 1992, in December 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In December 1992, at that time this building was held by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And for the benefit of the transcript, the witness pointed to the building on the right, the high-rise building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in what direction is the camera pointed in this photograph? In other words, are we looking approximately north south, east, west or what, from this high-rise building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It faces Nedzarici. From the side controlled by the BH army. It was -- the photograph was taken from the part that used to be under the BH army's control. This is Nedzarici, this is the institute, and over there is the centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would you agree with me that we are looking approximately due-west? If you disagree, please say so. Would it be more north-west?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: North-west rather.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness might now be shown Exhibit D1760, which is the map. Could the map be placed a little further up the screen -- I am sorry, the other way. Further down. Thank you. And could it please zoom in a little. Thank you. Stop there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, please take the pointer and point to the position of the car park which you just identified in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the photograph. Here, this is where this parking lot was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please point to --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because -- I am sorry. Because in front of the car park was the shopping centre. And then you have the car park and then the buildings behind it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please point to the Institute for Blind Children.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Institute for Blind Children is here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please point to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am sorry. We have so many questions about the car park. I don't know how is it relevant and why, as for the car park we never talked about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in fact the Defence asked a number of questions in cross-examination of the witness in relation to scheduled sniping incident number 25 as to the car park. So it has already been a topic of some interest to the Defence. Secondly, it assists in our end, the viewer, in photograph 1761, to understand where the car park and the institute are on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please point to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, before Mr. Ierace continues, we would like to hear your decision. Because Ms. Pilipovic did not mention the car park.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...give you a decision when you interrupted me. The objection is denied, but could you please, for our orientation, we do not need much assistance any more, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And I apologise for going straight into the next question. That was an oversight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In view of that, would you please point to the position, if it appears on this map, of the brigade headquarters, that is, your brigade headquarters, as of December 1992? And I think you identified it as the Ilidza Brigade.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Research Institute. Ilidza. Somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You point to an area which is --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wait, wait, please. Just a moment. Where are the spas, the watering places marked here. Energoinvest -- no, somewhere here. Yes, the watering -- no, just a moment. I won't take long. No, this is Terma Hotel. Somewhere here -- no, I am not quite sure. Somewhere here. Somewhere here is where the Ilidza Brigade should be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Perhaps you could now take again a blue pen.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is there a thinner one available?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, please place a blue cross to indicate the position of the brigade headquarters, and alongside --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like this, more or less?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. A bigger cross perhaps.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Alongside the cross, please put the initials "BRHQ."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: BR --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: HQ.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Incidently, you told us that you returned to your battalion in October 1993. Did you stay there for the duration of the armed conflict in Sarajevo, in other words, up until the end of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I think you told us that you would -- I withdraw that. Did the brigade headquarters change its position at any stage from September 1992 until August of 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the first brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first commander was Zoran Borovina and he was killed. And before that was a man whose name I had forgotten. And then Vladimir -- after Zoran, Vladimir --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the last name of the last commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the family name of Vladimir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radojcic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the first commander killed? Was that in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in May. No, no. Later, later. Or perhaps in May, mid-May. I am not sure about the date. I think when -- there were clashes in Otes and then he was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The name of the brigade commander who replaced him who you have -- which you have forgotten, does this job jog your memory? Was it Pero Despotovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first one was Pero Despotovic, and then it was Zoran, and then it was Vladimir Radojcic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Would you please place on the map now the location of your battalion headquarters.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The battalion headquarters was located -- battalion headquarters was located in the barracks which is -- which was here. This is where it was from 1992, and when I returned -- from 1992 until I was wounded. And then when I returned in 1993, the headquarters was moved to the Kasindolska Street. While the barracks is located here, so the headquarters of my battalion was here first.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please take the blue pen and outline the barracks where the battalion headquarters were first located. In other words, draw a line around the building, if it appears there, or the complex, the barracks complex.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is -- here is barracks. And this headquarters of ours was located here, here in this part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please turn the dot into a cross, if you can.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And alongside write "BAHQ."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you have written "BAHY." I think that will do. On the other side of the cross, please write the number "1."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That here?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, please place a cross where the battalion headquarters were from when you returned in October 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kasindolska Street. Approximately here. So I should put a cross, should I?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am just going to just use this opportunity while the witness is put the cross on just to remind you that we must discuss other witnesses in closed session. And there are certain little things to do with interpretation, so I am going to need a few minutes. I am just reminding you now so that tomorrow we don't find ourselves in a similar situation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ierace, how much time would you still need to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I should think some hours, Mr. President, with this witness. Perhaps we could just finish off the letters alongside the cross and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the left of the cross please place the number "2."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the right of the cross please write "BAHQ."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think for the transcript it is "BAHY."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP6 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have to deal with procedural issues in closed session. So we will do that now. We still need you tomorrow morning, so will you please come back to this courtroom tomorrow morning at 9.00 and do not speak to anyone about the testimony you have given in this court up until now. Madam Usher, could you please escort Mr. DP6 out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good-bye, Your Honours, and thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: See you tomorrow again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
